title: Breeding birds with temperature-organised ranges did not follow 1975-2025 warming more than other birds; residents moved more than migrants, and winter feeder birds moved north together
abstract: Question: is weak bird climate tracking caused by a small set of truly thermal species that the spatial benchmark hides? Data: North American Breeding Bird Survey (2,198 fixed routes, 1975-1994 against 2006-2025, May-July warming 0.81 C, 365 species) and, outside BBS, Project FeederWatch (805 fixed 1-degree cells, Dec-Feb, winters 1989/90-2002/03 against 2010/11-2023/24, 100-151 species), with GHCN_CAMS temperature. Method: for each species, binomial models of baseline occupancy gave a thermal organisation index tau (temperature against latitude, unique deviance shares). Tracking fraction f = observed move of occupancy-weighted temperature divided by the move that the species' own temperature model predicts. 2-degree spatial block bootstrap (200). Simulated truths validated the estimator. Plan written before results. Results: breeding f = 0.05 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.16). The high-tau third (median tau 0.75) had f = 0.05 (-0.14 to 0.26); a truth in which only the temperature part moves gives 0.85 there, full thermal tracking 0.95. All variants gave pooled f -0.17 to 0.17. Exploratory: residents and partial migrants f = 0.26 (0.14 to 0.46), full migrants -0.10 (-0.26 to 0.00); higher hand-wing index went with less tracking. Winter occupancy moved north by 42 km (19 to 55), about four times the 10 km of simulated full thermal tracking, but the move was shared by all species (common term -0.78 C) and not proportional to each species' expected move. Conclusion: the breeding gap is not set by a subset of non-thermal species; thermally organised species also stayed in place. Processes that act on residents or on the whole winter species pool are more likely. Limitations: tau is geographic and cannot separate temperature from habitat that follows isotherms; two periods only; small winter warming; FeederWatch network growth; migration groups chosen after first results.
